## ✨ Added

- Ships **Matrix Authentication Service (MAS)** inside the image, adding optional delegated auth and QR code device linking (MSC4108). It is strictly opt-in and off by default.
- QR device linking (MSC4108) is built on OAuth 2.0, which a plain Synapse with password logins cannot offer, and Synapse will not even start with `msc4108_enabled` unless authentication is delegated. Element showing **Settings → Sessions → Link new device** with a greyed-out *Show QR code* button and the note *"Not supported by your account provider"* is therefore correct behaviour on a non-delegated server, not a bug.
- With the switch off nothing changes: no config is written, no listener is opened, and the rendered Synapse config is byte-for-byte what it was before this feature existed (absent, not "delegation disabled"). Existing homeservers that pull `:latest` unattended are untouched.
- Enabling delegation needs three things, documented in the new README section 11: a second, empty PostgreSQL database; a second reverse-proxy host on port 8090 **with HTTPS** (MAS rejects plain-http redirect URLs and the container refuses to start otherwise); and one routing rule sending `/_matrix/client/*/{login,logout,refresh}` to 8090 while everything else keeps going to 8008.
- New template fields, all optional and all under Advanced: `AUTH_ENABLED`, `AUTH_PUBLIC_BASE`, `AUTH_POSTGRES_DB` / `_HOST` / `_USER` / `_PASSWORD`, `AUTH_ALLOW_REGISTRATION`, `AUTH_QR_LOGIN`, `AUTH_MIGRATE`, plus port 8090.
- Account migration into MAS: set `Auth: migrate accounts` to `true` and the container handles it on the next start. It runs during initialisation, before Synapse comes up, which is exactly the offline window the migration tool requires, except you cannot forget it and nothing can restart the homeserver halfway through. A pre-flight check runs first, then a dry run, then the real migration, and it refuses to continue at the first sign of trouble; if anything fails the container stops with the reason in the log rather than starting a homeserver with half-migrated accounts.
- Users keep their sessions and devices after migration: nobody is signed out and passwords keep working. It never runs twice, so leaving the field on `true` afterwards is harmless.
- Back up your database before enabling delegation: once the auth service has started and anyone has signed in, only a restore undoes this.
- Before enabling delegation, note what it changes: sign-in moves to the browser and Element hides the password field; login by email address stops working; password changes, email and account deletion move to the MAS web UI; `ADMIN_USER`/`ADMIN_PASSWORD` stop working entirely, and `admin-bootstrap` now says so and prints the `mas-cli manage` commands that replace them; encrypted bridges break; and existing accounts stay in Synapse until you run `syn2mas`, which needs downtime and is not practically reversible once anyone has signed in.

## 🎨 Design

- The banner wordmark and claim were refitted alongside the larger logo.

## ⚡ Improved

- Admin UI moves from `awesometechnologies/synapse-admin` (last released in March) to **Ketesa**, the maintained fork formerly published as `etkecc/synapse-admin`. It is a drop-in replacement at the same URL (`:8080/admin/`) and the only variant that understands a homeserver delegating auth to MAS, which matters now that delegation is possible.
- Component versions now live in the Dockerfile and nowhere else. The build workflow previously pinned Element Web and the admin UI in its own environment and passed them as build arguments, silently overriding the Dockerfile: the published image shipped **Element Web v1.11.92 and Synapse-Admin 0.10.3** while the Dockerfile advertised v1.12.23 and 0.11.4, and because Renovate's version trackers matched the Dockerfile lines, every dependency bump it opened for those two components changed nothing about the built image. Synapse remains the deliberate exception, resolved to the latest upstream release at build time. Renovate's data sources now point at the registries the Dockerfile actually pulls from rather than at same-named GitHub repositories with independent version numbers. This release therefore also delivers the Element Web update that had been stuck since the pins diverged.
- The "off means absent" guarantee is now a CI assertion, not an intention: the build fails if MAS configuration leaks into the render, if the pre-existing keys go missing, or if anything is listening on 8090.
- The arm64 build is no longer taken on trust: the MAS binary is checked for library resolution and executed once per target platform during the multi-arch build, so a broken arm64 binary fails the push instead of reaching a user.
- CI gained two further boot tests. One covers the delegated-auth path, asserting the three conditions Element checks before offering QR login, that MAS migrated its own database, and that its secrets survive a restart. The other performs a full migration: it creates a real account under plain Synapse auth, proves it logs in, migrates it, and proves the same password still works against the auth service - the assertion that matters, because a migration which leaves password hashes unusable looks entirely successful in the logs while locking every user out.
- Verified end to end before release: Synapse, MAS and Element in this image produce a real QR code behind a genuine TLS reverse proxy with the MSC4108 rendezvous channel serving, and an account created under plain Synapse auth survives the migration and signs in against the auth service with its original password.
- Licensing corrected: `LICENSE` has always been AGPL-3.0, but the image label claimed Apache-2.0 and the Docker Hub description claimed MIT; all three now say `AGPL-3.0-only`.
- README gained a troubleshooting entry for the failure mode that looks healthy from every angle: if `public_baseurl` does not match the address clients actually reach, QR linking fails with a generic error and nothing points at the cause. The manual migration instructions were also corrected, since the migration tool needs both Synapse config files (this container renders the database connection into the overrides file).

## 🐛 Fixed

- Failed startup checks now actually stop the container. s6-overlay defaults `S6_BEHAVIOUR_IF_STAGE2_FAILS` to "continue silently", which made every `exit 1` guard in the init scripts decorative: the startup script has claimed since v2.1.1 to be *"halting container start so the broken state is visible"* while s6 started Synapse anyway on a configuration already known to be broken, so a missing `SERVER_NAME` or a failed config generation produced a running-but-wrong container instead of a loud stop. It now stops with the reason in the log, and this affects every guard in the container, not just the new ones.
